title: Without agency, a character is just as much a story prop as a piece of furniture in the room.
use_cases: Use when a protagonist feels passive or reactive rather than proactive
Implement when the plot feels like a series of disconnected events
Configure when readers report a lack of emotional investment in the outcome
Use when developing stakes and consequences for character decisions
content: If there’s no true motivation behind the protagonist’s actions, and they don’t really have any reason to act in the novel, the plot becomes a series of “stuff that happens” and not a story. It’s hard for readers to care about the novel’s problems, because the protagonist doesn’t even care. The plot feels predictable because there are no impossible choices with real stakes being made, just a protagonist who’s following the road signs to the end of the book. And they aren’t even enjoying the scenery on the way. Here are four ways to strengthen the character agency in your novel:
